claim.summary: src/click/exceptions.py defines Click's exception hierarchy. ClickException (exit_code 1) is the base for user-facing errors. It has format_message() and show(). UsageError (exit_code 2) prints usage and a help hint. Its subclasses are BadParameter, MissingParameter, NoSuchOption, NoSuchCommand, BadOptionUsage, BadArgumentUsage and NoArgsIsHelpError. FileError is a direct ClickException subclass. Abort and Exit are NOT ClickExceptions: they derive from RuntimeError and are control-flow signals. Command.main in core.py (about lines 1571-1612) catches them. In standalone mode it calls e.show and sys.exit(e.exit_code). In non-standalone mode it re-raises ClickException and Abort, and returns Exit.exit_code.

interfaces.name: ClickException
interfaces.behavior: Base class (line 35). __init__(message) calls Exception.__init__, caches show_color = resolve_color_default() at construction (the context is gone by the time show runs), and stores message. Class attribute exit_code = 1. format_message() returns self.message. __str__ returns self.message. show(file=None) writes 'Error: {message}' via echo to file, or to get_text_stderr() if file is None, using the cached show_color.
edge_cases: message is not validated, so a non-str message would break __str__

interfaces.name: ClickException.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Returns self.message. Subclasses override it to decorate the message. show() uses it.

interfaces.name: ClickException.show
interfaces.behavior: Prints 'Error: <format_message()>' to the given file or to stderr. Color comes from the value cached at construction.

interfaces.name: UsageError
interfaces.behavior: Line 68. exit_code = 2. __init__(message, ctx=None) stores ctx and sets cmd = ctx.command if ctx else None. show() prints, in order: ctx.get_usage(), then a "Try '<command_path> <longest help option name>' for help." line only if the command has a help option, then 'Error: <message>'. Color comes from ctx.color. Without a ctx it prints only the Error line, with color=None.
edge_cases: ctx None -> no usage and no hint
help option disabled (get_help_option returns None) -> no hint
longest help name is chosen with max(key=len)

interfaces.name: UsageError.show
interfaces.behavior: Prints usage, the optional help hint, then 'Error: ...' to file or stderr. Uses ctx.color, not the cached show_color.

interfaces.name: BadParameter
interfaces.behavior: Line 114. __init__(message, ctx=None, param=None, param_hint=None). format_message() uses param_hint if it is not None. Otherwise it uses param.get_error_hint(ctx). If neither is set it returns 'Invalid value: {message}'. Otherwise it returns 'Invalid value for {hint}: {message}'. A sequence hint is joined with ' / ' with each item repr-quoted (_join_param_hints). A str hint is used as-is.
edge_cases: both param and param_hint -> param_hint wins

interfaces.name: BadParameter.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Builds 'Invalid value for X: msg', or 'Invalid value: msg' when there is no hint and no param.

interfaces.name: MissingParameter
interfaces.behavior: Line 159. __init__(message=None, ctx=None, param=None, param_hint=None, param_type=None). A None message becomes ''. format_message builds 'Missing {argument|option|parameter|<custom>} {hint}.{ msg}'. param_type falls back to param.param_type_name. If param is set, param.type.get_missing_message(param, ctx) is appended to the message: joined with '. ' if the message is non-empty, used alone otherwise. An unknown param_type is formatted as 'Missing {param_type}'. __str__ returns the message, or 'Missing parameter: {param.name}' if the message is empty.
edge_cases: empty message -> __str__ uses the param name, which is None if there is no param
param_type None and no param -> 'Missing None'

interfaces.name: MissingParameter.format_message
interfaces.behavior: See MissingParameter. Translates the known param types and appends the type's missing message (for example a Choice lists its choices).

interfaces.name: MissingParameter.__str__
interfaces.behavior: Returns self.message, or a 'Missing parameter: name' fallback when the message is empty.

interfaces.name: NoSuchOption
interfaces.behavior: Line 232. __init__(option_name, message=None, possibilities=None, ctx=None). The default message is "No such option 'x'." Possibilities are filtered with difflib.get_close_matches(option_name, possibilities) (default n=3, cutoff 0.6). format_message appends a sorted 'Did you mean ...?' suggestion (ngettext singular/plural) when matches exist. Stores option_name and possibilities (None when empty).
edge_cases: no close match -> empty list, no suggestion

interfaces.name: NoSuchCommand
interfaces.behavior: Line 268, added in 8.4.0. Same pattern as NoSuchOption: command_name, default message "No such command 'x'.", fuzzy possibilities via difflib, and the same format_message suggestion.

interfaces.name: BadOptionUsage
interfaces.behavior: Line 304. __init__(option_name, message, ctx=None). A UsageError that stores option_name. It is raised when an option is used incorrectly, such as the wrong number of values.

interfaces.name: BadArgumentUsage
interfaces.behavior: Line 323. UsageError subclass with no overrides. Raised when an argument is used incorrectly, such as the wrong number of values.

interfaces.name: NoArgsIsHelpError
interfaces.behavior: Line 332. __init__(ctx) calls super().__init__(ctx.get_help(), ctx=ctx), so the message is the full help text. show() echoes format_message() to stderr (err=True) with ctx.color, without the 'Error:' prefix or usage. It inherits exit_code 2.
edge_cases: show ignores a file argument's usage but passes file through to echo; err=True is used when file is None

interfaces.name: FileError
interfaces.behavior: Line 342. __init__(filename, hint=None). A None hint becomes 'unknown error'. ui_filename = format_filename(filename) (surrogate-safe) and the raw filename is stored. format_message returns "Could not open file {ui_filename!r}: {message}". exit_code is inherited as 1.
edge_cases: a surrogate filename renders as the replacement char U+FFFD

interfaces.name: Abort
interfaces.behavior: Line 362. A RuntimeError subclass, not a ClickException, with no custom attributes. In standalone mode, main prints 'Aborted!' (via _echo_aborted) and exits with code 1. In non-standalone mode it re-raises. KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError are converted into Abort in non-standalone mode.

interfaces.name: Exit
interfaces.behavior: Line 366. A RuntimeError subclass with __slots__ ('exit_code',). __init__(code=0) sets exit_code. It does not call super().__init__. Context.exit raises it (core.py:831). In non-standalone mode main returns e.exit_code. In standalone mode it calls sys.exit(code).
edge_cases: no message or args, so str(e) is empty

claim.error_conventions: ClickException subclasses are user-facing errors. main() prints them as 'Error: <msg>' and exits with exit_code. exit_code is 1 for ClickException and FileError, and 2 for UsageError and all its subclasses. UsageError, BadParameter, MissingParameter and the NoSuch*/BadOption* classes also print usage and a help hint when a ctx is attached. Abort and Exit are RuntimeError control-flow signals, not ClickExceptions. Message style is a capitalized sentence, usually ending with a period for the NoSuch* and Missing messages. User-visible strings go through gettext (_ and ngettext). Parameter names are quoted with repr, and multiple hints are joined with ' / '. Core also raises UsageError(message, ctx) from Context.fail (core.py:817) and Exit from Context.exit (core.py:831).

tests.how_it_asserts: A single test, test_file_error_surrogates. It builds click.FileError(filename='\udcff') and compares format_message() to an exact string with the replacement character and 'unknown error'. Plain assert, no fixtures. This is the only test I read. Other exceptions are probably covered indirectly in tests/test_basic.py, test_arguments.py and similar files, which I did not check.

extension_points.name: ClickException subclassing (override exit_code / format_message / show)
extension_points.what_could_attach: Custom user-facing errors: subclass ClickException, set exit_code, override format_message or show. Command.main handles them automatically (core.py:1597).

extension_points.name: UsageError.show
extension_points.what_could_attach: Custom usage rendering, such as a different help hint or JSON output.

extension_points.name: Command.main exception dispatch
extension_points.what_could_attach: A new handled exception type, or a global error reporter, added to the except chain.

extension_points.name: _format_possibilities / difflib suggestions
extension_points.what_could_attach: Shared suggestion formatting that other 'did you mean' errors could reuse.

gaps.description: There is no exit-code override on the constructor, so a custom code needs a subclass.
gaps.why_plausible: Exit already takes a code, so an optional exit_code argument is a small step.

gaps.description: There is no structured or machine-readable output, such as to_dict or JSON, for errors.
gaps.why_plausible: Errors already carry param, option_name and possibilities as attributes.

gaps.description: There is no fuzzy-match tuning (n and cutoff are fixed to the difflib defaults) and no suggestions for BadParameter or Choice errors.
gaps.why_plausible: NoSuchOption and NoSuchCommand duplicate the same possibilities logic, which could be factored out and parameterized.

gaps.description: Abort carries no message and Exit carries no message, so there is no custom 'Aborted!' text.

limitations: ClickException.message and show_color are Final, so subclasses cannot reassign them. show_color is captured at construction.
Abort and Exit are not ClickExceptions, so `except ClickException` does not catch them.
Exit.__init__ does not call super().__init__, so args is empty. Exit is slotted, but it inherits __dict__ from RuntimeError.
MissingParameter.__str__ and format_message differ: str gives the raw message or 'Missing parameter: name', while show gives the full formatted text.
NoArgsIsHelpError.show uses err=True, so its output goes to stderr only when file is None.
The only test for this module that I read covers FileError.format_message; other classes have no dedicated tests in tests/test_exceptions.
